q: Which footballer does Steve adore, partly because they're the same height?
f: Crouch's autobiography stole Steve's planned title, "Tall Stories".
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to the World Cup, 2010
ex: You identify with him don't you?
I love Crouchy. He's exactly the same height as me, six foot seven.
He's sort of lanky and awkward looking.

But brilliant. I mean, still a very, you know, let's not forget that he is playing in the national squad. He is a striker. He's got an excellent track record of scoring for England. Admittedly, maybe not in the super top important games…
He's like your role model. He's like your pin up isn't he?

q: Ricky read out a call for Company-style '50 most eligible bachelors' entries, suggesting Steve. Which magazine was compiling the feature?

ex: Right, Company magazine are compiling a 50 most eligible bachelors feature-
-for the May issue 2002, right, these are the requirements: single - that means available, not just unmarried; aged 20 to 30 - you're well in there.

q: Steve slagged off Sky One, saying that apart from The Simpsons it was WWF wrestling, cartoons and 'just the worst programmes'. He said it was like a station made by whom?
f: Steve listed WWF wrestling, cartoons "and just the worst programmes". Ricky agreed: "that's exactly the demographic."
ex: They have WWF Wrestling, cartoons, and just the worst programmes I mean it's appalling.
I have seen a bit of the wrestling, it's it's hilarious, it is hilarious.
But it's like a, like a station made by, a fourteen year old boy.
Yeah, well I think that, think that's probably what it is isn't it, I mean that, that's exactly the demographic, Do you like Sky One Karl?

q: Steve sarcastically said a 'lightweight frothy' Saturday afternoon Xfm show was 'exactly the place' to discuss what?
a: The desperate lonely future that's coming his way
f: Sarcasm: "a lightweight frothy entertainment show on Xfm on a Saturday afternoon is exactly the place" for his "desperate lonely future".
ex: Well. Karl I’m glad you’ve brought this up.
Because no, no- because I mean, for me, you know- a lightweight frothy entertainment show on Xfm on a Saturday afternoon is exactly the place-
-where I want to discuss the desperate lonely future that’s inevitably coming my way.

q: Steve's dad Ron asked his mother for a warm winter overcoat for Christmas. Why did she say he needn't worry about it?
a: His father would be dead soon, so he could have his
x: She'd knit him one out of old curtains
Overcoats were going out of fashion
He could borrow one off the neighbours
f: "Don't worry about that cause your father will be dead soon. Its alright, you can have his." Steve added that 20 years on, his dad is "still waiting" and freezing.
ex: Exactly, they basically stayed in bed. And er, it was one Christmas when erm, my grandmother said to my dad er, "What would you like for Christmas? What do you fancy for Christmas?" And this must have been.. I dunno, 20 years ago.

She said er, what do you er, what do you fancy for Christmas Ron? And he went, "Well, you know, I could do with a nice big kind of warm winter overcoat" She said, "Don't worry about that cause, don't worry about that cause your father will…
Which is good news. Good news for my grandfather. Less good news for my father he's freezing!

q: Steve noticed the exact moment Karl lost interest in Ricky's brain lecture. Which word made him pick up his phone?
f: "As you said the word 'symbolism', I noticed Karl drift away... pick up his mobile phone and start pressing buttons randomly." Ricky also risked "nomenclature".
ex: (laughs) Yeah, I know. Well, you started off by explaining it and I remember you mention I- because I was watching the two of you as you were describing it to him. You said, "Of course one side of the brain deals with, uh, symbolism." And…
And, I- I thought it was the word 'symbolism' that got him, and I noticed you-
Took you just a moment longer, and I think the first thing you said was, "When did I lose you?"
Yeah, I knew I'd lost him.
It is extraordinary- and he doesn't even try to disguise it!
I- I said "nomenclature" at one point as well...

q: In Moonraker, Bond punched a man through a window onto a piano. What did Steve say Bond quipped?

ex: There's one where he-in Moonraker he punches this guy-he's having a fight-he punches him through a plate glass window and he lands on a piano and Bond goes 'Play it again, Sam'.
What?! I always remember-there's one in one of the early films where he-
He throws a guy in the bath and electrocutes him by throwing in a uhm... a thing.
But I was thinking "You've just killed a man!"

q: Steve suggested his dad treat his mum to a makeover for their 20th wedding anniversary. What did Dad buy instead?
f: Steve: "It's a trowel, Dad!" Dad: "Do you think I should have got it engraved?"
ex: It's the thought that counts, right, so I suppose if you say that the thought that counts is the fact that he went and got anything at all, that counts, ok, fair enough, but he phoned me up, he said, "What shall I get your mother", right…

q: Why did Steve give up on buying condoms at the supermarket?
a: They were in a plastic cage he'd have to take to the checkout
x: The shelf alarm went off when he picked them up
His card was declined at the self-service till
He spotted an XFM listener in the queue

ex: No, no, no, no, no, no, no. I thought it was worth getting some condoms in. You know, it's Christmas party season and you never know when you're gonna run out of balloons. And I was weird because the condoms in the supermarket are…
Try it on, you know, in case it doesn't fit. Bring it back. Yeah, bring it back, yeah. Do you do alterations? Yeah, we do, yes.

Five pounds. So I'm trying to open this thing and this guy who works there, sort of this middle aged guy who works there, you have to take that to the checkout. So you can't open that yourself because I don't know, I still find it very…

q: Steve said he could eat anything on I'm a Celebrity. What did he say he couldn't cope with?
a: Life in camp: the lack of food and the uncomfortable bed
x: The heights in the physical challenges
Being voted for by the public
f: Steve admitted: "And I'd drive people spare, whinging and complaining."
ex: It wouldn't bother me. I could eat anything. I could do almost all of the challenges on that program, but I couldn't cope in the camp. I couldn't cope with the lack of food and the uncomfortable bed. That's all that would do my head. And…

I couldn't cope with any aspect of it except the physical challenges. I couldn't cope with sleeping with people snoring, the things crawling over you. Not so squeamish about that. Like snakes and things. That's alright. But the eating is…
It doesn't concern me. I don't know why. I don't see really what the difference in it, the texture is probably the same as lots of other things.

q: Steve was still under the weather when he back-announced a Stone Roses track. What did he call the band?
f: He also managed "10-storey love stong". Ricky: "Yeah, see, it's not as easy as it looks, is it?"
ex: Sure, sure, sure, sure, sweet, sweet, sweet, sweet, 10-storey loves stong- uhh- love stong? Ha, yeah, 10-storey love stong, from, uh, the Stone Doses.
Yeah, see, it's not as easy as it looks, is it?
It's not, it's not and I'll tell you, also because I'm a little under the weather still.
So (coughs) that's my, that's my excuse.

q: Steve allowed that Salman Rushdie might be a great man and a talented writer, but what did he think Rushdie needed to sort out?
f: Steve was baffled that Rushdie had a "stunning" wife: "he might be a great man and a talented writer... but, jesus. Do something with the beard."
ex: Well, I mean man alive. She's like a sort of - I think she's like a former Miss India or something, stunning.
Have you seen a picture of him?
I mean, he might be a great man and a talented writer and an intellectual fella but, jesus. Do something with the beard.

q: Karl said no cat was amazing enough to be worth a £5,000 operation. What did Steve sarcastically ask it should be able to do?

f: Steve pointed out that it's normally about people's affection for a cat they've had for many years.
ex: We went through loads of cats! I’ve told you before, as a kid, we got through loads. It’s not worth it and there’s no cat that is that amazing that you’d go, “Gonna miss that one. It’s never going to be the same cause it--”

What do you mean? What would it have to be able to do to be worth it? Wha- it’s normally to do with people’s affection for their cat. They’ve had the pet for many years. What do you mean, it should be able to juggle? Or do impressions and…

q: While they brainstormed ways listeners could sponsor them to 'Harm Karl', which gadget did Steve want to squeeze Karl's head inside?

I've always wanted one of those George Foreman grills, I've always wanted one of them
I know, but that's too out of the- that's too much innit?
We could just- we could- what if we just pressed his head inside it we don't have to- we don't have to put it on, just-
Don't put it on, see- see, yeah.
Just squeeze his head inside it.

a: One of the modern, sexy geeks

A geek, but a tall one

Not yourself. I mean-- I mean, you're not a geek in that sense, you're different.
I'm one of those sexier geeks, the modern, sexy geeks.

q: Karl insisted Steve's height had 'got him places' in his career. Where did Steve say it had got him?

ex: But it's got you places hasn't it?
I think, I think people give you bit more of a chance in, in your carreer and stuff, it's like...

q: At a New Year's celebration in Bristol, two girls approached 16-year-old Steve. What did they want?

To get him to reach the bar
To have their photo taken with him
f: "We can see you wherever you are… with the balloon." Ricky: "I love that, a landmark," and imagined pilots using Steve to find Bristol Temple Meads.
ex: Um, I was quite tall, I've always been like about 6 foot 7 for quite a while now and when I was about 16, erm.. I went to a big New Year's celebration in Bristol, where I come from, and they-- everyone kind of congregates in this big sort…
And they we-- (laughs) they said er, "you gonna be here for long?" And I went "well, maybe" and they said "it's just we've arranged to meet back at you

In about an hour." And I went "what do you mean?" and they went "well it's just 'cause we can see you wherever you are and.. don't worry, you can move around and stuff, we'll see you, with the balloon. Just arranged to meet some friends…

q: Steve said the idea of a rabbit with a beautiful woman like Jessica Rabbit left him feeling 'annoyed'. But what did he admit buying just after seeing the film?
f: Steve: "It is weird the idea of a rabbit having sex with a beautiful woman." Asked how that made him feel: "Annoyed."
ex: It is weird the idea of a rabbit having sex with a beautiful woman. That is the weirdest thing about it.
How does that make you feel?
If I'm honest. Yeah. But I bought some bunny ears just after I saw the film.

q: In The Flintstones, a giant rib tips Fred's car over at the drive-in. What did Steve wonder about the waitress?
a: Whether it was her first day on the job
x: Whether she was trying to get rid of Fred
Whether she'd ever seen a car before
f: Steve's logic: "either it's never been ordered before… or I think she should've realized". Ricky: "We're out of pig, we've got brontosaurus rib."
ex: …that huge rib and it tips the car over…
…was that her first day on the job?
Because… either it’s never been ordered before…
Yeah. “We’re out of pig, we’ve got brontosaurus rib.”

q: Steve went to an exclusive preview of Britney Spears' 'Crossroads'. Until when did he say he couldn't talk about it?
f: Or "the press people will go crazy." Ricky wasn't asking: "I would pump you for no reason ever." Karl: "We'll ask you in March."
ex: Rick, I su—I’m assuming you, you’d love me to do a little review of it now. I can’t because…
…it’s embargoed until March, I can only talk about it in March…
…otherwise the press people will go crazy.

q: Karl complained to the MD about "having me head squoze". Back on air after three months, what did Steve point out?
x: It's now in the Oxford English Dictionary
It only counts as a word in Manchester
It's actually spelt with two Zs

ex: I said, having me head squoze.
Squoze is still not a word. We've been away three months, it's still not a word.

q: Steve pictured fussy Ricky at the feeding of the multitude saying 'I'm not into the fish, JC.' What condition did Steve say Ricky would set for the bread?
a: It had to be Mighty White
x: It had to have the crusts cut off
It had to be from Greggs
f: Steve: "Unless that bread is mighty white, I'm not interested." Ricky added his fish orders: "take the head off... I can see a bit of spine."
ex: And you're there, and Jesus Christ has just fed 40,000 with some fishes and some loaves, you'd be going "I'm not into the fish, JC" and -
I'd say "take the head off, cook, really cook, take the skin off, there's, I can see a bit of spine, and while you're gutting -
Unless that bread is mighty white, I'm not interested.

q: Steve dropped his mobile on the tube. How did the old man who picked it up get his attention?
x: He tapped him on the head with it
f: Steve: "I thank you for pointing out I dropped my phone, but did you have to do the 'Lanky'?" Karl reckoned it worked, because Steve knew who he meant.
ex: You know I was on the--this is true--I was on the, eh, on the tube, right, coming in to meet Gervais the other day, and I was wearing a suit and my mobile phone slipped out of my pocket and it landed on the seat, and I didn’t realize this.…
And I was like “Well, I thank you for pointing out I dropped my phone, but did you have to do the ‘Lanky’?”
But you knew who he meant, I bet you turned around straight away. It worked.

q: Steve said his cagoule was stylish and he wore nothing underneath it. What did Ricky say that explained?
x: Why Steve shivers in the studio
Why nobody sits next to him on the tube
Why he never takes it off
f: Steve: "It's waterproof, Rick, and it's also stylish... it gets sticky in bad weather." His defence of the rustling: "It's sexy."
ex: It’s waterproof, Rick, and it’s also stylish--I wear nothing underneath. So it’s tight to the skin, it gets sticky in bad weather.
Ohhh is that why you, sort of rustle?

q: Ricky counted off the reasons their Churchill-on-coke chat wasn't libellous. What was Steve's reason number six?

ex: I’m asking, and we’re not, we’re not saying, you know, two (mumbles) fair, fair comment, um, uh, three we’ll say we were jokin’,
Five, we’re not condonin’ drugs in any way,
Six, this is Dermot O’Leary’s show.

q: Steve worried about his grandparents hearing the show. Who wanted to buy them a digital radio for Christmas?

ex: I was talking to my Dad the other day, he was saying, he lives in Bristol, my family live in Bristol and so they can't really listen to the show, and erm he said 'I was thinking of buying your grandparents a digital radio for christmas'.
'So they can listen to err, listen to your show'. Imagine them listening to that last link! And then me seeing them at Christmas 'Steve! You never told us you saw 2 blokes bummin’.

q: Imagining Karl on jury service, what question did Steve think the defence would use to weed him out?
a: "Have you heard of something called Rockbusters?"
f: Steve hoped the defence would "weedle out Karl at an early stage" by citing his Rockbusters clues.
ex: The only thing I can hope is that the defence attorney weedle out Karl at an early stage.
I object, have you heard of something called Rockbusters?

q: Steve picks Rockbusters winners whose names "tickle" him. Who won this week's prizes?
f: Steve insisted: "there's nothing amusing about that." Ricky: "Suckling takes the prizes."
ex: Alright, well, fair enough and well done to, you know, I'm always a fan of names that for some reason just strike me or tickle me.
And this week the lucky winner is Dave Suckling.
I, there's nothing, there's nothing amusing about that.
Okay, so well Suckling wins it. Suckling takes the prizes.

q: Karl's pet magpie got violent and pecked his head. What was Steve's theory?
a: It mistook his head for a tree because of the hollow sound

It was after crisps in his pocket
It was jealous of his Grifter
f: Ricky reckoned the sun was glinting off Karl's thinning hairline. Steve went with "the hollow sound".
ex: They saw a glare and thought 'i'll have that'.
Yeah, or as it was for pecking away at mistook it for a tree
'cause of the the noise, yeah, the hollow sound.

q: Ricky squeezed Karl's head so hard that Karl "definitely heard something crack". What did Steve say the noise really was?
a: Karl thinking, with the cogs starting up
f: Steve: "I think that was you just thinking, Karl... I think the cogs just started to..."
ex: But I squeezed it yesterday and Karl went 'I definitely heard something crack.'
Because I'm trying to see how hard I can squeeze it.
Yeah. I think that was you just thinking, Karl.
To be fair. I think the cogs just started to... No, I mean, I think there is a danger, because I think there is a danger that you could you could squeeze it too much.

q: Steve kept his postcards boring in case the postman read them. What might he write from a bawdy lads' holiday?
a: "Nice. Sunny. Got meself a lovely pair of shorts."
f: Steve: "I'd keep the truth, Rick! For when I got home."
ex: No, but af- as you’re posting them, as you were posting them through the letter box, you’d have a quick look, wouldn’t you, to see what was- what they’re up to. Because that’s why I never used to write anything of any interest on a…
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
I’d just write some, you know, “Nice. Sunny. You know, got meself a lovely pair of shorts.”
Something like that. You know, I would- I’d keep the truth, Rick!

q: As a glasses wearer, what drives Steve mad when people ask to try his glasses on?
a: They always say "Oh! I can't see a thing!"
x: They always leave thumbprints on the lenses
They say "Now I look like you!"
f: Steve: "What were you expecting? X-ray vision!? No!"
ex: Tell you what frustrates me. Can I just say, as a glasses wearer, this is just a-a note to everyone out there who isn’t a glasses wearer. When people ask constantly to try on your glasses- “Can I try on your glasses?" and they try them on…
If you’re a glasses wearer, you don’t want people asking to try on your glasses.
But I think they don’t realize that--

q: A woman walked Steve to the front of the club queue and told the bouncer "this is Steve Merchant, Office". What did the bouncer say?
a: "I know who he is, we're not letting him in"

"Prove it. Do the David Brent dance"
"Only if he signs my Office DVD"
f: Afterwards Steve had to lean over the rope to pose for camera-phone photos with the people who were being let in.
ex: So I thought, well, you know. Well, the thing is, we were out and I was a bit frustrated and I thought, you know, we may as well try everything. So I stand there. And my friend goes over and he has a word, and he comes back and he says…

So the guy, the guy takes me and my mates, right? This girl, she takes us, we walk past everyone else, right, to the front of the queue, right? She goes up to the guy, she says, this is Steve Merchant, office. The guy goes, I know who he…

q: When Steve was about 10, his dad got a reversible jacket for Christmas. What was the problem with it?
a: Both sides looked almost identical: beige and white just swapped round
x: It was pink on one side and orange on the other
It only reversed from the waist down
The sleeves fell off when you turned it inside out
f: Beige body, white arms; inside out, "beige arms, white body... looked almost identical!" Steve said reversible jackets were all the rage "for about 25 minutes".
ex: ... 10 -- and I thought this was Dynamite -- I was so jealous. It was a reversible jacket.

Well, I know, I mean they were all the rage for about 25 minutes and um -- and -- and it was a me.. But what was great about it -- it seems to me with a reversible jacket what you want is you want, say, checks on one side and just, say…
Whereas this one obviously, little bit cheaper -- Mum not splashing out a huge amount. It was kind of -- had a beige body, white arms -- turned it inside out, beige arms, white body. It..

... looked almost identical! And I could never quite understand when he was ever going to utilize that -- when people would think -- do you know what I mean -- when it.. When he would, he walk to a party? They'd say, you know..

q: Ricky hoped the poster for their comeback would say "Back by popular demand!" Which phrase did Steve say was his favourite?
f: Ricky agreed: "As we're doing it for nothing. We want a little bit of pat on the back, don't we?"
ex: I'm hoping to put that on the poster "Back by popular demand!"
Well, I'm hoping it's "By overwhelming public demand", which is my favourite.
Yeah , exactly. Yeah. Yeah. As we're doing it for nothing. We want a little bit of pat on the back, don't we?

q: Steve mocked people praising Tolkien for creating his own language. Who did he say comes up with a new word every week?
f: Steve: "Whoopee, Karl comes up with a new word every week that he's made up. He's not a genius!!" Ricky cited Karl's "frightnenness".
ex: Yeah, i think that's how it's described in the book. But this is the other thing, they go "Oh Tolkein, JRR Tolkein, he's a genius. You know he created his own language?". Whoopee, Karl comes up with a new word every week that he's made up.
Yeah. That bloke...the bloke. A look of frightnenness came across his face.
Frightnenness. Yeah. Karl's new word. Although you know Shakespeare introduced 1200 words the English language, apparently.

q: When Steve's family watched The Elephant Man, what did his dad say that 'cheapened the film' for him?
a: "Wouldn't he make an amazing novelty rucksack"
x: "He'd be handy at a football match"
f: While the rest of the family were nearly moved to tears, his dad went "wouldn't he make an amazing novelty rucksack."
ex: This is true, my dad watched that once, and we were watching it, and my mum and my sister and that were all quite moved by it, almost moved to tears, thinking it was a wonderful example of man's inhumanity to man and all those things, and…
And it cheapened the film for me, I've never had that sort of emotion since...

A beer mat with names on it

The back of a Gareth Gates poster --
-- with some blue tack on it.

ex: So I wrote my name on, and um - put down three quid. 'Cause a lot of people were giving fivers
But I thought, you know, I'm not made of money, it's Christmas. I got to buy gifts and stuff.

q: Steve asked the sponsorship girls, "Aren't you supposed to do the things?" What did the girl say?

q: Ian Camfield said the Blur track was "Good Song". What did Steve think at first?

q: Steve recalled a Feng shui woman who said his office needed a £25 crystal to get the negative chi out. What happened when he refused to pay that?

She knocked it down to twenty quid

It was surprisingly convenient that she had a number of different crystals that apparently did the same job.

a: The haircut of the bloke from the Kaiser Chiefs
x: The free CD on the front cover

The letters pages... People complaining about the haircut of the bloke from the Kaiser Chiefs.
It's not a pressing concern. Move on.

q: Which venue did Steve reckon would happily pay the £12,000, as 'apparently they've already got his ball'?

ex: Have you got his ball? Well no, the Albert Hall's got one, his mother's got the other, so I don't know...
See the Albert Hall, I would have thought, would probably be paying that £12,000, because apparently they've already got his ball.
Yeah, they've got one of his balls, so...
They've got one of his balls in the Albert Hall. His Mother's got the other....
...but if they got the todger as well...
If they can track down the one his mother's got, they would have a complete set of Hitler's...

ex: The Rolling Stones: Beast of Burden. Can I just take this opportunity, Rick, to say to Sir Mick Jagger: Happy 60th birthday this year, Mick.
Happy 60th birthday this year? Was it today?
Well otherwise you'd be saying "happy birthday" to everyone every day.
No, no, no, no, no. Because I don't know Mick Jagger, do I? So I'm just taking the opportunity in case you happen to be listening today to wish him a 60th... happy 60th. Or someone who knows him...

q: Steve mocked Chris Moyles for 'rather hilariously' changing Martine McCutcheon's 'This Is My Moment' to what?

ex: Do you remember when Moyles rather hilariously changed the words of 'This is my moment' by Martine Mccutcheon to 'this is my motor'?
We listened to it though didn't we?

q: Ricky offered a golf song for Duran Duran: 'something down the fairway'. What did Steve suggest instead?
f: Minutes after mocking Moyles's golf song competition, Ricky and Steve couldn't resist joining in themselves.

Um... something down the fairway or something? If they wrote that?
Girls on the putting green? Or something?

q: Karl didn't want futon buyers coming to his house. Steve suggested meeting them at the end of his street and doing what?

Driving them round in circles first

ex: I've got an idea, what about if you meet them at the end of your street, you blindfold them-
Like they do when- when terrorists take the negotiator to the uh-
And um- and so you can do that and in- and so, you know they- they could piece together, maybe where you live.

q: Steve put his orthopaedic chair up for sale at £25. What deal did he offer if the buyer was a charity?
x: They could have it for free
f: Ricky said high-flier Steve would just give it away to a good cause. Steve did promise "it is in good condition cause I haven't really sat on it."
ex: I mean um- because though Steve's such a high flier, I mean, if it really is a good cause he'll just give it to ya.
Let's not rush into anything, Rick. I like to assess each case individually.
Certainly, certainly if you are a charity then- then I might go for 20 quid, I can- you can take it off my hands for 20 quid.
Um- but otherwise 25 and I'll tell you-

q: Steve went to see Bruce Springsteen at Wembley. Why did he feel he was 'in trouble' at the gig?
a: He was the trendiest person there
x: He was the only one not in denim
He was the youngest there by 30 years
He was the only one who knew the new songs
f: Steve reckoned Bruce fans also bought tickets for Mark Knopfler and Dave Gilmour ("of Pink Floyd without Pink Floyd").
ex: And uh- he started with that song we just played. And it was dynamite. I mean he never let up. Almost 3 hours, he rocked the joint. He's 53 he was sliding across- it was pure rock and roll. Pumping our fist, sliding across the floor on his…
… then I'm in trouble. D'you know what I mean? And there was- some of the people there- I imagined, you know on Amazon.com um- it says like, "People who bought X also bought Y."
And I think people who bought tickets to Bruce probably bought tickets for Mark Knopfler.

q: Listeners emailed huge cut-and-pasted reams about the origins of sumo wrestling. What did Steve ask for instead?
a: Bullet points with key words like "arse" and "sumo"
x: A single sentence in big capital letters
A voicemail read out by their mum
f: Ricky: "Not that I'd read the bullet points, either. You'd read them to me." Steve would also accept a diagram, a sketch or a flick book.
ex: But they’ve sort of cut and pasted a huge ream of information from the web. Thanks very much, but we need bullet points or not-not- don't bother. You’re wasting our time, frankly, with any, with any- too many sentences, proper grammar.…
Yeah. Not that I’d read the bullet points, either. You’d read them to me.
Exactly. But exactly. Your concentration would lapse so quickly--
There just needs to be key words, you know, “arse”, “sumo”, things like that.

q: Steve said a friend of his would spend millions, if he won them, bringing back which fashion accessory?
f: Steve: "you can make such an entrance with the cape." Ricky added that it needed a cane.
ex: Well this is the thing... but I... cause my friend always said if he won millions of pounds, he'd spend it all trying to bring back, as a fashion accessory, the cape.
The cape! See I quite like the cape.
Because you can make such an entrance with the cape.
A cape and a cane, yeah, and a top hat.... I wish people had to wear hats now. I see it on...

q: According to Steve, at what number did Tom Cruise, the world's top box office star, scrape into the VH-1 list?
f: Steve reckoned it was "a list drawn up by people who just sat at home and looked along their video and book collection."
ex: Oh no, they don’t really count. It tends to be, they don’t feature. I mean Mickey Mouse is in there, uh, what do you make, what do you reckon – Tom Cruise, higher or lower, Tom Cruise is the number 1 box office star in the world?
Just about scraped in there... it really is a list drawn up by people who just sat at home and looked along their video and book collection.

q: Steve told Karl about the very first contraceptive diaphragms, used centuries ago. What were they made from?
f: Ricky added that "the more selfish man turned them inside out."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Medicine · 2008
ex: ...if we go back, just get back on message. There are of course a number of extraordinary developments. You may obviously be aware, Karl, that the first contraceptive diaphragms centuries ago were citrus rinds half an orange rind for…
I mean the more selfish man turned them inside out.
I believe that's also still being used in parts of Manchester.

q: At the Sonys, Karl quietly slipped Steve an envelope. What was inside?
a: £200 cash for his XFM DJ set
x: A fan letter from Phill Jupitus
f: Steve: "The tax man won't know about that, cash in hand." After Ricky's sarcasm about the tax office, he quickly promised: "I'll declare it."
ex: You know I did that storming set the other night...
This was down at a little club, in case you weren't aware of it.
Anyway went to The Sonys the other night, Karl Pilkington sidles up to me, slips me an envelope.

q: Steve boasted his DJ set at an XFM night 'went down a storm'. What did three girls tell him as he walked to the toilets during his set?
f: Ricky was not impressed: "What cos you played records in a certain order?"
ex: Hour and a half, me and my friend split the time on the decks, what, what was the word you just used?
We went down a storm. Right, three girls, I was walking to the toilets during my set, three girls went 'you are a genius'...
Right da-, whathisname, Dane Bowers... Zane Lowe?
What cos you played records in a certain order?

q: Steve arrived at the airport in a chauffeur-driven car, buzzing the window down like a big shot. What did the check-in woman tell him?
x: He was booked on the wrong day
He'd been bumped down to economy
f: Steve pleaded: "It's business-class, what can you do?" She could fly him out, but he'd "have to just turn around and come back."
ex: --I get to the airport in my chauffeur-driven car. Right, I'm sat there, I'm phoning people - my mum and dad, you know, "You'll never believe what I'm off to. Just- just in a car. Just in a chauffeur-driven car", and I get to the airport…
And I'm just there- I'm just, sort of, buzzing the window down, handing it to her, buzzing it back up like, "I don't want to talk. Check the passport--"
"--take my luggage, I don't want to discuss things, you know who I am." And she hands the passport back through the window, she says, "It's expired."

I went, ("Fool" Voice) "Eewhaa- what do you mean?" She went, "It's expired." I thought- I said, ("Fool" Voice) "It's business-class, what can you do? Can you do anything?" and she went, "No, we- we can send you to America but eight hours…

q: Steve rang Ricky to admit he didn't know passports expired. What was his reasoning?
x: He'd only ever used it once
Nobody had ever checked it before
f: Steve then asked, "How old do you have to be to know that?" and, plaintively, "When will I know all these things?"
ex: He called me- he called me, right, he said, "Rick, I've really mucked up-", "Go on.", he went, "My passport expired." I went, "Awww. So what are you gonna do?!" He went- he said, right, I c- he went, "I didn't know passports expired."

I went, "What do you mean?", I went- he went, "Well, your driving license doesn't." I went, "What are you talking about?!" He said, "How old do you have to be to know that?" He said- he said, "When will I know all these things."
(laughing) He went, "When will I know all these things?"

q: Steve claimed that what a lot of people don't realise about Mozart is that, in his spare time, he used to...
f: Specifically "musical crimes. Plagiarism issues, things like that." Claire: "Oh we've come full circle now, haven't we?"
ex: What a lot of people don't realise-
It was like Alan Jones. It was all over by the time he was eleven.
What a lot of people don't realize about Mozart was that he also, in his spare time, used to solve crimes.
Yeah. That was why he was so... musical crimes. Plagiarism issues, things like that.
Oh we've come full circle now, haven't we?
We have indeed, we've brought that right back.

q: Steve told a tube worker at Finchley Road that a flap of buttons was swinging open on his train. What was the worker's reply?
a: "How they gonna check if they don't know what carriage it's in?"
x: "You'll have to fill in a form"
f: Steve was livid: "I just wanted to smack him in the face... I'm just trying to help you out and that's our attitude".
ex: They don't, it's pretty grim, anyway so I went up to this guy and I said, excuse me mate, I was just on this train there and there was a flap open and I could see all these buttons and things, he went 'right', I was like, yeah I just…

He went 'what carriage was it', I went well I don't really know what carriage it was, maybe at the next stop someone should come and check, he went, 'well how they gonna check if they don't know what carriage it's in?'

And at that point, I thought, I just wanted to smack him in the face, you know, I'm in a hurry, I've got no reason, there's no gain for me about telling this, it's not gonna help me out in anyway, not financially, nothing, I'm just trying…

q: Forty minutes after the bomb scare call, a policeman finally checked the suspect bag. What did he do?
a: Found rubbish inside and threw the bag at them
x: Blew it up in a controlled explosion
Took it away as lost property
Ate the sandwiches he found inside
f: He said "there's your bomb for ya" and drove off. Steve: "what lesson are you teaching us about being good citizens..."
ex: So, anyway, listen, he calls the police right and so after a while, you know it was like forty minutes later and I think the police do a good job, I'm not trying to be down on the police, it's a good job, and I respect the police, but this…
What did you do, presumably you reported him did you?
No, of course not, what's gonna happen, you know, it's not...

q: Steve said he never mouthed off at firemen in his youth. What was he too busy doing?
a: Asking "can I try on your helmet?"
x: Asking to slide down the pole
Asking for a go in the fire engine
f: Steve: "Cos I never did stuff like that... I was too busy saying 'can I try on your helmet?'" Cue a Ricky cackle.
ex: I think you should publicly apologise to the fire brigade now.
Oh, I'm so sorry, so sorry.
Cos I never did stuff like that...
I was too busy saying 'can I try on your helmet?'

q: Steve watched a lot of Columbo while he was off sick. What was his theory about the detective?
x: He nicks his cigars off the suspects
f: "Do you not think that Columbo looks like he smells?" Steve reckoned he's too busy solving crimes to clean his clothes.
ex: I was watching er, the one thing I did watch all, all week was Columbo which seems to be on constantly. I was watching Columbo and I know you’re a fan of Columbo Rick?
My, one of my favourite programmes of all time.
I’ve taped it. Oh, right, I just thought you were gonna talk about it.

q: Mocking pointless board games and toys, Steve pitched a new product "from Mattel". What was it?
a: A stick for clanking along fences
x: A cardboard box to sit in
f: Ricky named it "Fence Stick" and did the advert kid: "Oy, Nan! Nan, that's my Fence Stick!"
ex: "New from Mattel: A Stick! Simply run along clanking it against a- uh, a fence or a metal grate--"
"It's Fence Stick!" and a picture of a little a- "Oy, Nan! Nan, that's my Fence Stick!"
(Laughing Slightly) "That's my Fence Stick!" Do you know what I saw in, uhh- in a shop recently? The board game of "Cold Feet"--

q: Steve said that, being under thirty, his dad's mates in the pub would never ask him to do what?
a: Taste their pint of bitter to see if it's off
f: "Taste that. See if that- is that off?" Steve: "My opinion is the last one they would consider."
ex: If you’re under thirty, you don’t even- it’s like, I was thinking today, if I was in a pub with my dad and, say, his mates and they’re all, sort of, forty or fifty, there is not one of them that would turn to me first with a pint of bitter…
No. They wouldn’t. They wouldn’t want your opinion.
They would never consider me. My opinion is the last one they would consider.

q: When Ricky said Karl had made Daltrey, Entwistle and the rest of The Who look like fools, what punning reply did Steve make?
f: Karl had argued that every song needs "a little bit of realism". Ricky and Steve agreed it was "a fair point", and Steve couldn't resist the pun.
ex: But, but the thing is with all songs or stories, there's got to be a little bit of realism to it. D'ya know what I mean. Why bother putting money in it? Just let him hit the buttons if he's happy.
That is great. Yeah. Well, I think you've Daltrey and Entwistle and the whole crew look like fools.
Yeah, they Won't Get Fooled Again.

q: In the Human Body guide intro, Ricky called Steve an award-winning writer and a graduate of which university?
f: Ricky said he was joined by "Stephen Merchant award-winning writer and graduate of the University of Warwick." Karl got a very different introduction.
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The Human Body · 2010
ex: As Aldous Huxley once said, man is an intelligence in servitude to his organs made from the same stuff as algae, the human body has evolved into the most complex organism in the universe. An animal with power of introspection, conceiving…

q: Steve was fairly sure a woman pinched his arse at Green Park tube. When Ricky warned him about pickpockets, what did Steve say?
a: Even if she'd taken his wallet, it would've been money well spent

He keeps his wallet in his sock for that reason
He'd have chased her down the escalator
f: Steve admitted it wasn't "a hundred percent corroborated" but he was "fairly certain", and he thought about putting up posters around Green Park.
ex: Uhm, I was on the tube coming down, and I don’t ah… I don’t want sound arrogant, I don’t want to sound pushy, but uhm… I was at Green Park, and I’m fairly certain, Rick, it’s not a hundred percent corroborated, I’m fairly certain… that a…
But the—there’s a lot of pock—uh, pickpockets around Green Park so be careful.
No no no no no, no no no no no, my wallet was still there.
But even if it wasn’t, you know, that would’ve been money well spent but…
…but… but the… but the wallet was still there so how, what do you think of them apples? Eh?

q: Ricky said homeless people recognise him. Steve said that was his demographic: people who do what?
a: Watch TV through the window at Dixons
x: Read old copies of The Sun on the bus
Listen to Xfm on a radio they found
f: Ricky played along, imagining them saying "Ricky Gervais is on... pop the telly on."
ex: Although I get recognized by homeless people and… are they, I don’t know where they…
But you’ve got to remember that’s very much your demographic, Rick…
…people who watch TV through the window at Dixons.
…yeah, in Dixons, yeah, they go, “Ricky Gervais is on…”

q: When Ricky asked what Karl's pool-dwelling spider was called, which famous swimmer did Steve suggest it might be?
f: Steve's guess got an instant follow-up from Ricky: "Is it bald?"
ex: There must be a reason, if anyone's watching, please if you were watching that program, I don't know, I don't know about this spider, what's the name of the spider?
I'm not sure, but it did say...

q: What was the first programme on Steve's new plasma TV, and what nearly took his eyeballs out?
x: Antiques Roadshow - a valuer's bow tie
Ready Steady Cook - Ainsley Harriott's grin
f: Steve said the glow was "like x-rays". Ricky imagined Dickinson turning to camera: "he just turns around, takes the cornea off."
ex: The problem was it took me forever to wire it in. I thought I'm not going to pay for someone to wire it up, you know. So it took me about three hours to wire it in and it was huge. And I got it switched on, and the first program that was…
Ahh, it was incredible. Oh it was like, its like x-rays. Its extraordinary, the glow.
So close. I know, this huge plasma screen with this orange thing coming at ya. (jshhh) And he keeps, and he keeps turning to the camera doesn't he?
Yeah. Of course. With that grin.
Just to get ya. Yeah, he turns away, you get a bit closer. They go, "what's he doing?" And he just turns around, takes the cornea off.

q: Karl reckoned Neil Armstrong's words didn't matter, anything would have gone down in history. What did Steve suggest Armstrong could have said instead?
x: "Is it me or is it chilly up here?"
"Pass the cheese, it's made of it!"
f: Karl's theory was that quotes "don't really matter" and "it's more the situation that you're in rather than the quote itself". Ricky's offer: "I'm as happy as a pig in dust!"
ex: And um, I was saying you know, quotes - don’t really matter
It’s more the situation that you’re that you’re in rather than the quote itself
So, like Neil Armstrong, if he’d have said.. What, um, you know…
“I’m as happy as a pig in dust!”
Yeah, that would’ve still gone down in history as like the thing that Neil Armstrong said wouldn’t it?

q: As Karl explained that the mum in 'The Shining' saw "Redrum" in the mirror, what did Steve joke she thought it was?
f: "She thinks he's offering racing tips." Karl was presenting it, said Ricky, like Jonathan Ross on 'Film 2003'.
ex: No. And he said, uh- he wrote down “Redrum.”
On the back of the door.
And his mam wakes up and thinks, “What’s he doing?”
She looks at him and she goes, “Oh” and then she looks in the mirror and sees “Redrum” in the mirror--
Right. She thinks he's offering racing tips.

q: According to Ricky, what does Steve look for on a wedding gift list?
f: Ricky: "they look down the list and they find things under £25." Steve didn't deny it, saying the wedding list "drives me insane".
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The English · 2009
ex: Although I know you were annoyed Steve. Steve doesn't like to part with money. I don't know what the politically correct term is. Stingy c*** inn'he , I mean, he's f***ing mean. And if he ever has to spend out on like a wedding gift to…

Oh, it drives me insane. Well, firstly, I'm annoyed about the wedding list. I don't know when that's come along, because I don't know why I can't just bring maybe something I've made at home. Why is there got to be a list of stuff?

q: When Steve's dad needed a heavy winter coat, what did Steve's Gran tell him to do?
a: Wait and have his father's coat, as he'd be dead soon
x: Buy one in the January sales
f: Steve's dad "must have been waiting ten years for that winter coat." Ricky: "You can see where Steve got it from!"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The English · 2009
ex: So he must have been gutted. But my father, when my father needed a winter coat, a big heavy winter coat, and he was thinking of buying one and my Gran said "No don't worry about that, Ron, you can have your father's winter coat." And he…
I love the fact he waited.
You can see where Steve got it from!

q: Steve wanted to tell a 14-year-old girl chatting on her phone in the cinema to hang up. Who did he suspect she was talking to?
a: Gavin, asking to meet behind the bike sheds
x: Her mum, asking what she wanted for tea
Her mate, describing the film to her
A boy called Darren from the chippy
f: Unless it was "your broker in Hong Kong saying, 'The big deal is about to go through'", Steve wanted her to "Put the phone down!"
ex: Climbed over a few seats, sat down - ha, brilliant! - next to a teenaged girl, on her mobile phone.
And she's on there, she's chatting away-
Steve does an impression of a teenaged girl on a phone

Da na na na na, "I'll meet you after," da da na na na. And I wanted to grab the phone off her and say, "I'll be honest with you, you're 14, and unless this is your broker in Hong Kong saying, 'The big deal is about to go through,' - which…
Put the phone down!" People who are on the phone in the cinema!

q: What annoyed Steve about the free Christmas TV listings supplements the papers had started giving away?
a: About half the listings just said 'to be confirmed'
x: They were mostly adverts for sofas
f: Steve: "Who is planning their film and TV watching this early?" Ricky's party excuse: "It's to be confirmed, but I can just say this - I won't be at the party".
ex: But when they bring them out this early, you open it, and you think "oh I want to see what films are on" and stuff, and you open it, and about half of the listings are "to be confirmed". It's an utter waste of time, but it's like, who is…
Yeah, 3 weeks in advance, going "Oh I'd better not make any...", well unless it's an amazing thing on telly...
"Are you coming to our party? We've got one, Friday 29th", "Err, I dunno, I've got to watch something on the TV, there's a good film", "What is it?", "Not been confirmed yet, but I'm just..."
"It's to be confirmed, but I can just say this - I won't be at the party", yeah.

q: Steve claimed that in his classy household they'd often switch off the TV and do what instead?
a: Listen to a concerto on Radio 3
x: Read Dickens aloud by the fire
Play chess and discuss the news
f: He then admitted: "I don't know what a concerto is - I've just said that word." Ricky reckoned it was "just a posh word for concert".
ex: Whereas you see, we, in our house, of course we'd often just switch off the TV, we'd just perhaps listen to a concerto on Radio 3.
Ooh, yeah, we weren't allowed to turn the telly off, really.
I don't know what a concerto is - I've just said that word. I assuming....
I know what a concerto is, it's like a, just a posh word for concert, innit?

q: When Karl said several XFM colleagues backed his Hitler theory, which brainboxes did Steve sarcastically say now worked on the show?
f: Steve mocked "the big thinkers that are in this office" and "the brain boxes" before asking: "Or is it Paxman?"
ex: The big- yeah, the big thinkers that are in this office.
Cause, I mean, Magnus Magnusson works on the show now, doesn’t he?
Or is it Paxman? Was it Jeremy Paxman?

q: Steve argued that a far more common phrase on the show than 'There's this hairy Chinese kid' would be what?
f: The pair kept going with other classics: "Karl, you're a fool", "Karl, where have you been?" and "Karl, you're a loser".
ex: Uhhhm, first thing that spring- sort of, sprang to mind was, uh, "There's this hairy Chinese kid."
But more- more commonly it would be something like "Karl, you're an idiot"--
Yeah, "Play a record you ignorant fool"--
"Ooh, what do you mean? You let us down again. You should have been here."--

q: Steve held up other radio shows with professional presenters who have talent and can string a sentence together. Which DJ did he say he was thinking of?
f: Ricky had just apologised for a not-so-slick show. Steve's example of the polished alternative: "You know I'm thinking Chris Moyles." Ricky: "I'm bored with those people... I think we need a little bit of Karl."
ex: But I think there's so many shows that are, you know, nowadays on radio and I think there's- there's a lot of stuff that's heavily formatted, you know, and there's well- you know- I don't know, presenters who are professional and got some…
And ability to sort of sting a sentence together.
You know I'm thinking Chris Moyles.
Yeah. But I mean I'm bored with those- those people who-
-you know, uh- I think we need a little bit of- a little bit of Karl.

q: When Karl started picking holes in God's design of the toad, how did Steve defend God?
a: He's got a lot on his plate and took on too much

He copied the design from another planet
He left toads to an apprentice
f: "Don't start slagging God off. He's got a lot on his plate." Ricky added: "Particularly in one week."
ex: The fact that there are still toads around is a testament to that defense working, that's all I'm gonna say. Ok? If the toad had died out, you'd have a point. But they're still around. It works. Alright?
Don't start slagging God off. He's got a lot on his plate. He- I mean he basically, I think he took on too much.

q: Karl moaned that he'd had to carry the computer up the stairs on his way to the recording. What did Steve say really happened?
a: His girlfriend carried it, then Karl handed it to Steve
x: Ricky carried it while Karl held the door
Karl left it in the taxi
The cab driver carried it up for him
f: Steve says Karl handed him the computer and said "steve, carry this." Steve's verdict: "That's already a lie."
ex: Yeah, but I had to get here. It's been raining.
Come up the stairs. I had to carry the computer.
Yeah, well, that's not entirely true because your girlfriend was carrying it. I saw her outside.
And then you handed it to me and said, steve, carry this.

q: When Ricky read the 'Track Ending Now' warning out on air, why did Steve tell him off?
a: He was giving away the secrets of radio
x: Karl hadn't cued up the next song

ex: Nirvana, Man Who Sold the World. Karl’s all confused ‘cause it didn’t tell you it’s ending, did it. What is that, a sort of glitch in the –
Careful they might start swearin’. You know what they’re like.
Yeah, and all their habits and that.
Yeah, it says Track Ending Now.

Stop talkin’ about it! That’s – that’s, you’re givin’ away all the secrets, of radio, an’ that. People think it’s like an old piece of vinyl that we’ve put on a needle, you know, like those old bits of footage of Tony Blackburn. That’s…

q: Ricky said smallpox was once found in a 'marked' yogurt pot in a university freezer. What did Steve wonder?
a: If someone had put their name on it so nobody ate their yogurt
x: If it was well past its sell-by date
If it was one of those Fruit Corners
If someone had given it marks out of ten
f: Steve asked if it was marked "because they don't want someone to eat their smallpox yogurt". Ricky put it down to "an admin problem".
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Medicine · 2008
ex: Well there was a bit of a scandal a few years ago, I think 10 years ago, where in a university laboratory, someone came across a marked yogurt pot in deep freeze that had smallpox in it. That was a hangover from the seventies
When you say it was marked, was it like someone's put their name on it because they don't want someone to eat their smallpox yogurt?
No no no, I think they looked into it and it was the deep frozen smallpox virus.
They just let it in the fridge?
Well I think so yeah it was an admin problem.

q: Karl said germaphobes who won't even shake hands are "going to die of something". What did Steve suggest it would be?

s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Medicine · 2008
ex: Yeah. So, you know, it's always there, colds and flus everywhere. That's interesting, isn't it? That more sort of colds are spread through shaking hands than people, you know, just taking in the air. Because people sneeze into their hand…
Yeah, that's going too far, because they're going to die of something. You can't be that paranoid. Gotta get on with your life

q: Steve started his own mobile disco at about 14. What was it called?

ex: Guess what, when I first started the mobile d-, disco, this was when I was about 14, we just we didn't really go out touring and we would just do it for like people's parties and stuff, and we were called the Rock and Roll DJs.
We drew it on some er, on some see-through paper and put a light behind it, Rock and Roll DJs.

q: Two blokes in a white van tried to sell Steve speakers at a petrol station. Which shop did they claim to work for?
f: Their story: undelivered goods could be sold off on the way back. Ricky: "That happens a lot. Yeah. Dixons must love that!"
ex: Exactly. So they - so I couldn’t believe my luck! So uh, they drove behind the garage, the little sort of garage bit at the back, and I went round there, sort of casually went round there, sort of locked the car and went round there. Um…
Then that’s really good for Dixons.
That happens a lot. Yeah. Dixons must love that!

q: When Karl talked about quitting, why did Steve say the whole show would have to end without him?

A canoe and a glass eye
A parrot and a wooden leg

ex: Yeah, but I remember when I-- that's not really-- it was just about objects and odd things in odd places. I used to work for a magazine when I lived in Bristol, and I remember the editor said to me once, he said: "Oh, we got a page-- we…

Yeah, live chicken in a hotel room. And that was just left behind. And a false leg. I mean, I don't know who lose-- I don't know who leaves behind a false leg. I mean, presumably you'd notice if you didn't have your false leg, because…

ex: Like somehow that will hide it, that will disguise the name. But it’s... my friend Rufus, his parents lived in a place called Folkingham, this is amazing when he was growing up, they lived in Folkingham, they moved, to a village, called…
Perhaps you come from an amusing town or street!
Hello mate! Fingringhoe or Folkingham? Ohh.. Well, that’s my business.

Ricky would do all the work

He phones up, "How is he today?", "He's fine.", he goes, "Okay. Aw, I'm freezin'."
